submission.justification: Sensor-T3 has the best unirradiated resolution (6.0 um), but its hit efficiency at 2e16 neq/cm^2 is 82.0%, which fails the hard 97% requirement. At that fluence, full depletion can no longer be reached at maximum bias. Sensor-T1 and Sensor-T2 both pass: T1 at 98.5% and T2 at 99.2%. Of the two, T1 has the better resolution, 9.0 um versus 14.0 um for T2, based on the 2025 simulation at 150 um, unirradiated. That makes Sensor-T1 the choice. Thickness is set to 150 um because it is the only thickness with resolution data, it is inside the 50-300 um range, and the efficiency was measured on that sensor type. Caveats: no simulation tool was available for this task, so thickness was not optimized. Also, the resolution figures are for unirradiated sensors, and the records do not show whether the irradiation test used 150 um sensors. Before freezing the design, a thickness scan and a resolution measurement after irradiation are recommended.

requirements.requirement: Goal: best possible single-hit spatial resolution
requirements.evidence: Among sensors that pass the efficiency requirement, T1 has the best resolution: 9.0 um vs 14.0 um for T2 (2025 simulation, 150 um, unirradiated). T3 (6.0 um) is excluded. The thickness was not optimized, and resolution after irradiation was not measured.

requirements.requirement: Sensor must be one of the three candidate technologies

requirements.evidence: The 2026 irradiation and test-beam campaign measured 98.5% for T1 at 2e16 neq/cm^2.
